_meta.description: Company universe — one record per investable name across all 13 verticals. Fields: ticker, name, vertical, chain_layer, geo, structure, thesis_note, conviction. Conviction re-ranked 2026-05-30 on a chokepoint-ownership spine (3 reserved for near-monopoly / sole-source / hardest-to-replace owners). Living doc — enrich over time.

themes_registry.label: EDA & IP
themes_registry.blurb: Design tools + CPU/IP licensing — the head of every silicon chain.

themes_registry.label: WFE Equipment
themes_registry.blurb: Semicap equipment — litho, deposition, etch, metrology, ALD, MOCVD, bonders.

themes_registry.label: HBM Memory
themes_registry.blurb: High-bandwidth memory + its test/stacking/probe chokepoints.

themes_registry.label: CoWoS / Adv. Packaging
themes_registry.blurb: Advanced packaging — CoWoS interposer, hybrid/TC bonding, ABF substrates.

themes_registry.label: Co-Packaged Optics
themes_registry.blurb: CPO + silicon-photonics packaging — TSMC COUPE, FAUs, optical engines.

themes_registry.label: 1.6T Optics
themes_registry.blurb: 800G→1.6T optical-module transition; transceivers, lasers, photodiodes, DSPs.

themes_registry.label: PIC Enablers
themes_registry.blurb: Substrate + equipment monopolies upstream of every PIC — SOI, InP, MOCVD, wafer bonding.

themes_registry.label: 800V HVDC / Wide-bandgap
themes_registry.blurb: 800V-DC AI racks inheriting EV/solar's SiC/GaN supply chain.

themes_registry.label: Agentic East-West Traffic
themes_registry.blurb: Server-to-server interconnect surge — switches, sockets, colo, fiber.

themes_registry.label: Humanoid OEMs
themes_registry.blurb: Listed humanoid robot makers — Tesla, UBTech, Hyundai/Boston Dynamics, XPeng, etc.

themes_registry.label: Humanoid Actuators
themes_registry.blurb: The cost-dominant joint layer — reducers, screws, motors, drives, bearings.

themes_registry.label: Industrial Robotics
themes_registry.blurb: Industrial arms, cobots, AMRs — Fanuc/Yaskawa/ABB/KUKA + cobot leaders.

themes_registry.label: Sensing & Perception
themes_registry.blurb: Vision, lidar, depth, IMU, force/torque/tactile — the robot's nervous system.

themes_registry.label: AR & Smart Glasses
themes_registry.blurb: Near-eye displays, waveguides, light engines, AR SoCs, device assembly.

themes_registry.label: China Localization
themes_registry.blurb: Domestic Chinese substitutes — EDA, WFE, memory, motion, sensing.

themes_registry.label: Japan Chokepoint
themes_registry.blurb: Japan-dominated material/equipment chokepoints — wafers, resist, optics, reducers.

themes_registry.label: Agentic Utilities (SW)
themes_registry.blurb: Infrastructure software that wins on agent usage, not token price — CDN/comms/observability/IAM. Per Citrini SOTT June 2026, reclassified as in-scope AI infra.

themes_registry.label: Edge AI / On-Device
themes_registry.blurb: Local inference inflecting after years of lag. Memory cost is the binding constraint; light/private tasks move on-device, complementary to cloud.

themes_registry.label: Flash / HBF (DRAM Tax)
themes_registry.blurb: NAND offloads weight storage from scarce DRAM. SK Hynix + SanDisk HBF standard (Feb 2026) validated by Apple AFM 3; HBM4-compatible, 8–16x capacity.

themes_registry.label: Token Panic
themes_registry.blurb: Subsidized AI ending; per-token costs become visible as labs flip to usage-based pricing. Drives demand for efficiency, cheaper inference, open-source models.

themes_registry.label: EU Chips Act 2.0
themes_registry.blurb: June 3 2026 act: dropped market-share target, pivoted to demand-side procurement + small-country pivot (Sweden/Finland/Norway/Poland). €15–30B for European DRAM.

companies.name: Synopsys
companies.thesis_note: Half of the EDA duopoly; broadest design+IP flow. Gates all advanced design. Export-control on/off lever to China.

companies.name: Cadence Design Systems
companies.thesis_note: Other half of EDA duopoly; emulation (Palladium) strength. High-margin recurring; AI design tailwind.

companies.name: Arm Holdings
companies.thesis_note: Dominant CPU IP; royalty model into every phone + growing datacenter. Arm China JV is a control wrinkle.

companies.name: Alphawave Semi
companies.thesis_note: High-speed SerDes + HBM PHY + UCIe IP — the connectivity layer of AI chip design. M&A target interest.

companies.name: Empyrean Technology
companies.thesis_note: China's leading EDA firm; cannot match full-flow leading-edge but the national champion under sanctions pressure.

companies.name: ASML Holding
companies.thesis_note: Sole EUV maker — the single deepest chokepoint in tech. High-NA ramping at Intel/Samsung. The toll booth of leading-edge.

companies.name: Applied Materials
companies.thesis_note: Broadest WFE portfolio (~18% share); also leads hybrid bonding into advanced packaging. Service base recurring.

companies.name: Lam Research
companies.thesis_note: Etch + deposition leader; critical for 3D NAND and gate-all-around. China exposure a swing factor.

companies.name: KLA Corporation
companies.thesis_note: Near-monopoly in process control/inspection — yield is the gating economic variable on every new node.

companies.name: Tokyo Electron
companies.thesis_note: Japan's WFE champion; coat/develop (with ASML litho) + etch/deposition. Core to every fab line.

companies.name: VAT Group
companies.thesis_note: Near-monopoly in vacuum valves inside every deposition/etch tool — a hidden single-source subsystem chokepoint.

companies.name: Advantest
companies.thesis_note: ATE duopoly with Teradyne; HBM/AI complexity lengthens test time = direct AI test-demand leverage.

companies.name: MKS Instruments
companies.thesis_note: Process subsystems (gas, vacuum, RF, lasers) + advanced packaging chemistry (Atotech). Broad WFE+packaging exposure.

companies.name: NAURA Technology
companies.thesis_note: China's largest WFE maker (~#8 globally); etch/deposition/clean. The localization bellwether ex-lithography.

companies.name: ASM International
companies.thesis_note: Leader in Atomic Layer Deposition — the gating process for the FinFET→GAAFET (nanosheet) transition (film conformality on 3D surfaces). Underappreciated vs ASML/AMAT; ALD steps rise sharply at GAA nodes. Owns ~25% of ASMPT.

companies.name: Onto Innovation
companies.thesis_note: Process control / metrology + advanced-packaging inspection; HBM and chiplet complexity drives more inspection steps per wafer. Smaller semicap leveraged to the AI/HBM capex cycle.

companies.name: AIXTRON
companies.thesis_note: MOCVD monopoly (70-90% share; >85% GaN) — grows the III-V epi layers behind every photonics laser AND the GaN power devices for 800V HVDC. Dual photonics + GaN tailwind the market underprices. A hidden German chokepoint.

companies.name: SUSS MicroTec
companies.thesis_note: Near-monopoly in photomask cleaning (~90% at TSMC) + ~50% of Samsung/Micron HBM temp bonding; its XBS300 does the laser-to-wafer heterogeneous integration every SiPh foundry (GFS/Tower/UMC) needs, plus hybrid bonding. ~70% of revenue is advanced packaging.

companies.name: Veeco Instruments
companies.thesis_note: The only credible MOCVD competitor to AIXTRON (together a duopoly) — III-V epi for photonics + GaN power; also laser annealing / ion beam. Mid-merger with EV-exposed Axcelis (ACLS); weaker setup than AIXTRON but cheap optionality.

companies.name: Wonik IPS
companies.thesis_note: Korean front-end deposition equipment maker; GEMINI PECVD platform used in Samsung 3nm GAA + 2nm logic process. ~50% revenue from Samsung Electronics. Tool move-in happens BEFORE wafer revenue — early-cycle beneficiary of Samsung's Taylor (TX) leading-edge build-out + memory P4/P5/M15X/Yongin investment cycle.

companies.name: TSMC
companies.thesis_note: ~90%+ of <5nm + the CoWoS packaging chokepoint + COUPE photonics. The keystone of the entire AI hardware universe.

companies.name: Samsung Electronics
companies.thesis_note: Only IDM spanning DRAM/HBM/NAND + foundry + OLEDoS. Samsung Foundry is being repriced as the most realistic global second source for leading-edge logic — Tesla's $16.5B Taylor 1 deal anchors a 2H27 ramp; Taylor 2 in active 2nm review; Marvell's Google memory-adjacent ASIC slotted on Samsung 4nm (mid-2027 launch). HBM4 qual recovery is the memory leg.

companies.name: Intel
companies.thesis_note: High-NA EUV lead customer (14A). US foundry turnaround optionality; execution + external-customer wins are the swing.

companies.name: UMC
companies.thesis_note: Mature-node foundry; display drivers, RF, power. Exposed to China mature-node overcapacity but stable cash flows.

companies.name: GlobalFoundries
companies.thesis_note: US/EU specialty foundry — automotive, RF, power. Western-supply-security premium; not leading-edge.

companies.name: SMIC
companies.thesis_note: China's foundry champion; 7nm via DUV multipatterning powers Huawei Ascend. Capped at ~7nm by export controls.

companies.name: Shin-Etsu Chemical
companies.thesis_note: Largest 300mm wafer maker (with SUMCO ~50%+); also photoresist. Quiet upstream Japan chokepoint under TSMC itself.

companies.name: SUMCO
companies.thesis_note: Second 300mm wafer giant. AI capacity ramp tightens wafer supply; pure-play wafer cycle exposure.

companies.name: Soitec
companies.thesis_note: ~80% of silicon-on-insulator wafers — the substrate every photonic IC (incl. TSMC COUPE) is built on; Shin-Etsu licenses its Smart Cut. Priced as a mobile/RF cyclical; SiPh + LNOI/SmartSiC is the underpriced optionality. Cross-link to Optical.

companies.name: Tower Semiconductor
companies.thesis_note: Specialty analog/RF/power foundry investing ~$650M to triple silicon-photonics shipments by mid-2026 — a SiPh-foundry beneficiary of the CPO wave alongside GFS/UMC. Geographically diversified.

companies.name: SK Hynix
companies.thesis_note: HBM leader (~62%), Nvidia's lead supplier; MR-MUF process edge. The single best pure-play on the HBM bottleneck.

companies.name: Micron Technology
companies.thesis_note: Only US memory maker; HBM3E ramp overtook Samsung (~21%). US-supply-security + HBM growth dual thesis.

companies.name: Kioxia Holdings
companies.thesis_note: Japan NAND leader (ex-Toshiba); relisted on the TSE Prime Market Dec 2024 (ticker 285A). NAND cycle + AI storage tier; HBM-era enterprise-SSD demand.

companies.name: SanDisk
companies.thesis_note: WD NAND spinoff; enterprise SSD + AI storage. Commoditized but cyclical-leverage play.

companies.name: Phison Electronics
companies.thesis_note: Controller leader; AI inference local-storage + memory-expansion angle. Taiwan-listed controller pure-play.

companies.name: ASE Technology
companies.thesis_note: World's largest OSAT (~45% of top-10); CoWoS overflow + advanced packaging ramp. Direct AI packaging leverage.

companies.name: Amkor Technology
companies.thesis_note: #2 OSAT; $7B Arizona advanced-packaging fab with Apple/TSMC — the US back-end reshoring play.

companies.name: BE Semiconductor
companies.thesis_note: Hybrid-bonding equipment leader — enables sub-10µm 3D stacking. High-margin chokepoint of advanced packaging.

companies.name: ASMPT
companies.thesis_note: Bonders + advanced packaging tools (TCB, hybrid bonding). Leveraged to the packaging capex cycle.

companies.name: Ibiden
companies.thesis_note: Top ABF substrate maker; high-layer-count substrates for big AI dies are supply-constrained. Japan substrate chokepoint.

companies.name: Unimicron
companies.thesis_note: ABF substrate leader (~22%). AI-die substrate demand + capacity tightness. Taiwan substrate pure-play.

companies.name: Ajinomoto
companies.thesis_note: Makes the ABF insulating film itself — a hidden near-monopoly upstream of every IC substrate. Food-company optionality.

companies.name: Kulicke & Soffa
companies.thesis_note: Bonding equipment; advanced packaging + thermocompression transition. Cyclical assembly-capex exposure.

companies.name: FormFactor
companies.thesis_note: Near-duopoly (with Micronics Japan) in MEMS probe cards that contact thousands of 40µm-pitch HBM microbumps for known-good-die screening — the hardest test in the industry. Nvidia tightening HBM test standards is a direct tailwind.

companies.name: Powertech (PTI)
companies.thesis_note: Memory back-end (DRAM/HBM/NAND test, near-full utilization) + PiFO — a leading CoWoS-L alternative — and FOPLP; >NT$40bn 2026 capex; Meta reportedly interested in PiFO. A second-source advanced-packaging play as CoWoS stays tight.

companies.name: Cohu
companies.thesis_note: Automated test handlers + the Neon HBM inspection tool + Eclipse handler (active thermal control for ~3,000W AI processors). Leveraged to AI-chip + HBM test complexity; cyclical.

companies.name: Hanmi Semiconductor
companies.thesis_note: ~90% share of HBM4 thermo-compression (TCB) bonders — a Korea HBM-packaging chokepoint. But the HBM4E→HBM5 shift to hybrid bonding (BESI/ASMPT) is a structural risk; SK Hynix co-developing 2nd-gen hybrid tools with Hanwha. A chokepoint-at-risk.

companies.name: Doosan Tesna
companies.thesis_note: Korea's #1 system-semi wafer-test OSAT; revenue scales with Samsung Foundry utilization. KRW171.4bn capex for Apple CIS line (2H26) + KRW190.9bn for Nvidia LPU package-level test (Q4 2026 ramp) + Pyeongtaek Plant 2 shell (Nov 2027) sized for Marvell's Google-bound 2nm ASIC. AI-infra cycle replacing the mobile cycle.

companies.name: Samsung Electro-Mechanics
companies.thesis_note: Dual thesis: (1) FC-BGA captive substrate vendor for Samsung Foundry — every new 4nm/3nm/2nm chip accumulates SKUs here; industry-wide FC-BGA capacity tight. (2) MLCC content per Rubin Ultra ~1.8M units (~90x H100); 24-week lead times; the 800V-DC transition adds ultra-high-voltage MLCC demand (>10x ASP premium). Top-tier alongside Murata, TDK, Taiyo Yuden.

companies.name: LG Innotek
companies.thesis_note: SiP (System-in-Package) substrates for smartphones/wearables/TWS/AR-VR. Survivor-economics play: every major substrate maker is reallocating capacity toward AI-server FC-BGA, leaving SiP undersupplied — same pattern as MLC NAND (Macronix) and DDR4 (Nanya). Margins could lift from ~9.5% (2026) toward ~14% (2028).

companies.name: Aehr Test Systems
companies.thesis_note: Burn-in test specialist — stresses chips at heat to filter infant-mortality defects. Google placed a $41M follow-on TPU package-level burn-in order (FY27 deliveries) — first hyperscale-AI design-in. Sonoma (package) + FOX (wafer) platforms; future vectors: SiC, GaN, flash, HBM, silicon photonics. Insurance policy on very expensive silicon.

companies.name: Nvidia
companies.thesis_note: ~80-90% merchant AI silicon; CUDA moat; Blackwell→Rubin. Also NVLink, BlueField DPU, Jetson Thor, $4B optics. The hub.

companies.name: Advanced Micro Devices
companies.thesis_note: MI300→MI400 (HBM4, 2nm) + Helios rack; the credible #2 merchant accelerator. ROCm software is the gating risk.

companies.name: Broadcom
companies.thesis_note: Designs Google TPU, Meta MTIA, OpenAI ASIC + dominant switch silicon + CPO. The diversified AI-infra compounder.

companies.name: Marvell Technology
companies.thesis_note: AWS Trainium + Microsoft Maia ASICs + optical DSP. Nvidia took a stake around NVLink Fusion. Custom-silicon #2.

companies.name: Alchip Technologies
companies.thesis_note: Turnkey backend ASIC design at advanced nodes (AWS et al.). Taiwan picks-and-shovels on the custom-ASIC wave.

companies.name: Global Unichip (GUC)
companies.thesis_note: TSMC-affiliated ASIC design service; advanced-node turnkey. Leverage to custom AI silicon proliferation.

companies.name: Cambricon
companies.thesis_note: China AI-chip champion; benefits from domestic-compute mandate + Nvidia export curbs. Capped by SMIC/HBM access.

companies.name: MediaTek
companies.thesis_note: Co-designs Google's TPU v7 (Trillium) — a custom-ASIC co-design win beyond the AVGO/MRVL duo; underappreciated AI leverage after weak mobile. Top mobile/edge SoC vendor.

companies.name: Arista Networks
companies.thesis_note: Ethernet leader for AI back-end networks; Ultra Ethernet beneficiary vs InfiniBand. Hyperscaler-concentrated.

companies.name: Astera Labs
companies.thesis_note: PCIe/CXL retimers + fabric switches + AECs — the AI-connectivity pure-play; UALink optionality. Premium valuation.

companies.name: Credo Technology
companies.thesis_note: ZeroFlap AECs dominant top-of-rack; signal-integrity at 224G. High-growth connectivity niche.

companies.name: SiTime
companies.thesis_note: MEMS timing/oscillators inside 1.6T modules, NICs, switches and accelerator boards — content ~doubles to ~$2/module at 1.6T, ~25-50% of a growing TAM. Exclusive MEMS-oscillator supplier for Apple's in-house 5G modem. Architecture-agnostic AI-timing play.

companies.name: Celestica
companies.thesis_note: Hyperscaler white-box networking + AI server ODM. Cheaper torque on the cluster-fabric buildout.

companies.name: Accton Technology
companies.thesis_note: Leading white-box switch ODM for hyperscalers. Taiwan networking-hardware pure-play.

companies.name: Cisco Systems
companies.thesis_note: Networking incumbent; SiliconOne G300 (102.4 Tbps) switch silicon + AgenticOps/Splunk observability. Beneficiary of the agentic 'east-west' traffic surge + enterprise-networking refresh, though less AI-pure than Arista.

companies.name: Hon Hai (Foxconn)
companies.thesis_note: Largest AI-server/rack assembler; GB200 NVL72 builds. Scale leader; thin margins but huge AI revenue ramp.

companies.name: Quanta Computer
companies.thesis_note: Major AI-server ODM; rev +66% YoY. Direct beneficiary of hyperscaler GPU-server demand.

companies.name: Wiwynn
companies.thesis_note: ~50% of hyperscale AI-server procurement; rev +149% YoY. The purest Taiwan AI-server ODM play.

companies.name: Super Micro Computer
companies.thesis_note: US AI-server leader; liquid-cooled rack-scale. Governance/accounting overhang is the key risk to weigh.

companies.name: Vertiv Holdings
companies.thesis_note: Datacenter power + thermal leader; liquid-cooling inflection (GB200 mandates it). Picks-and-shovels on power/cooling wall.

companies.name: Delta Electronics
companies.thesis_note: World-leading DC power supplies + power management; 48V-to-chip transition. Quiet AI-power compounder.

companies.name: Monolithic Power
companies.thesis_note: Power-management silicon for GPU boards; content-per-GPU rising with 1kW+ accelerators. High-quality compounder.

companies.name: Asia Vital Components
companies.thesis_note: Cold plates + thermal modules for AI servers; liquid-cooling ramp. Taiwan cooling pure-play.

companies.name: GE Vernova
companies.thesis_note: Gas turbines + grid for behind-the-meter AI power. The cross-link from datacenters into the energy supply chain.

companies.name: Wolfspeed
companies.thesis_note: Pure-play silicon carbide; runs the world's only commercial 200mm SiC fab (Mohawk Valley) + demoed the first 300mm SiC crystal (only Coherent is close). Post-Ch.11, debt-free — levered to 800V-DC AI racks inheriting the EV/solar SiC supply chain. Turnaround risk.

companies.name: onsemi
companies.thesis_note: Broad-line SiC + silicon power; EV/solar capacity now finding a second AI-datacenter cohort (800V HVDC). Also a CMOS image-sensor maker (robotics/auto). Valued on the soft EV cycle.

companies.name: STMicroelectronics
companies.thesis_note: European IDM; SiC power + analog/MCU. 'Supply-chain inheritance' play — EV-validated wide-bandgap capacity now serving AI power. Also a silicon-photonics play: its PIC100 platform (TSV + SiPh) anchors a multi-year, multi-billion AWS datacenter-optics + laser-driver contract. Diversified, EV-cycle exposed.

companies.name: Navitas Semiconductor
companies.thesis_note: Pure-play GaN (+SiC) for high-frequency power conversion; GlobalFoundries-partnered and aligned to Nvidia's 800V-DC architecture. Small, volatile, high-beta on the power-semi theme.

companies.name: ASPEED Technology
companies.thesis_note: ~80% of general server BMC chips and ~100% of Nvidia Hopper/Blackwell GPU-rack BMCs (87 per NVL72) — an 'ASML-like' near-monopoly chokepoint. BMC TAM raised to ~65M units by 2030 on AI-server + agentic demand; content/ASP rising. Re-rank candidate (possible conviction-3).

companies.name: Equinix
companies.thesis_note: Largest interconnection/colo REIT (~70% colo revenue); Equinix Fabric on-demand interconnect (500k+ interconnects, ~60% of large new contracts AI). The convexity is interconnect, not just floor space — a beneficiary of agentic east-west traffic. Cross-link to Networking.

companies.name: Digital Realty
companies.thesis_note: Major DC REIT; ServiceFabric software-defined interconnect closing the gap to Equinix. Levered to colo demand + AI interconnect. A facility-layer landlord, not a hardware chokepoint.

companies.name: LOTES
companies.thesis_note: ~35% of CPU sockets + memory/quick-disconnect liquid-cooling connectors; content-per-server rising as pin counts go 5,000→7,000+. Now raising prices (vs historical cuts); Vietnam capacity for non-China AI-server supply.

companies.name: FIT Hon Teng
companies.thesis_note: Foxconn interconnect arm; ~40% CPU-socket share + 224G/448G connectivity, high-speed cables, M-CRPS power connectors. Cloud/DC revenue mix climbing ~16% (2025) → low-30s% by 2028.

companies.name: Coherent
companies.thesis_note: Vertically integrated lasers (EML) + transceivers + SiC optics. Nvidia ~$2B supply commitment. Optical chokepoint owner.

companies.name: Lumentum
companies.thesis_note: EML/DFB lasers + datacom optics; Nvidia ~$2B commitment locks supply. Leverage to 1.6T + laser scarcity. Also the MEMS-mirror OCS system supplier to Google's TPU pods (Project Apollo, R300/R64) — direct TPU-buildout leverage.

companies.name: Fabrinet
companies.thesis_note: Builds transceivers for Nvidia/Cisco/Coherent (first $1B quarter). Thailand-based, geopolitically diversified picks-and-shovels.

companies.name: MACOM Technology
companies.thesis_note: >60% share of 200G photodiodes used in 1.6T modules + TIAs/drivers; architecture-agnostic across pluggable optics, copper-linear and near-packaged optics. A clean 1.6T-transition pick-and-shovel.

companies.name: Nokia
companies.thesis_note: Via the Infinera buy, owns the only vertically-integrated InP fab in the West (Sunnyvale; CHIPS-backed San Jose/Bethlehem fabs) — ICE-D intra-DC optics vs Lumentum/Coherent. Also a $1B Nvidia 6G investment. A 'forgotten' optics turnaround.

companies.name: FOCI Fiber Optic
companies.thesis_note: Assembles the fiber-array unit (FAU) for TSMC's COUPE CPO platform (Himax-partnered, Himax holds ~5%); the fiber-to-chip handoff for Nvidia Rubin-era CPO. Small/illiquid (TPEx-listed).

companies.name: Ciena
companies.thesis_note: Coherent optical transport + DC interconnect (DCI); acquired Nubis for scale-up/out optics. Levered to the longer-reach links between increasingly distributed AI campuses. Citrini's original optics call.

companies.name: Furukawa Electric
companies.thesis_note: DFB laser chips (capacity +500% by 2028; Nvidia locked long-term contracts) + MT/MPO ferrules + rollable-ribbon cable + CPO ELS/TOSA modules. Moving up the value chain into CPO light sources.

companies.name: Sumitomo Electric
companies.thesis_note: MT/MPO/MMC ferrules (~30% share) + EML/CW-LD lasers + InP substrates (2.4x capacity by 2028) + fiber-to-chip attach for CPO (FlexBeamGuidE); Nvidia SiPh ecosystem partner. Owns the fiber-to-chip interface.

companies.name: Applied Optoelectronics
companies.thesis_note: 800G/1.6T pluggables (Microsoft-heavy, ~29% of revenue) scaling toward CPO lasers. Demand > supply, but a concentrated/fragile customer base and a heroic CPO ramp — crowded, valuation-sensitive.

companies.name: Semtech
companies.thesis_note: Industry-leading transimpedance amplifiers (TIAs) + laser drivers; acquired HieFo for proven InP lasers/gain chips. Positioning for 1.6T/3.2T + CPO/near-packaged optics. Architecture-agnostic optics-component pick.

companies.name: InnoLight Technology
companies.thesis_note: World #1 transceiver maker; with Eoptolink ~60% of Nvidia 800G. China assembly dominance — a quiet supply exposure.

companies.name: Eoptolink
companies.thesis_note: Fast-rising 800G/1.6T transceiver maker; gaining Nvidia share. China optical-module growth play.

companies.name: Mitsubishi Electric
companies.thesis_note: One of <5 EML laser makers — the deepest optical chokepoint. Diversified conglomerate; small but strategic laser unit. Also makes MELFA industrial robots + a servo/PLC automation ecosystem — a robotics-adjacent angle.

companies.name: Harmonic Drive Systems
companies.thesis_note: Historic near-monopoly in harmonic reducers for robot joints — designed into Western humanoids. China localization is the risk.

companies.name: Nabtesco
companies.thesis_note: ~60% of precision RV reducers for mid-large industrial joints. The high-torque reduction-gear chokepoint.

companies.name: THK
companies.thesis_note: Linear motion (ball screws, rails); planetary roller screws are a humanoid bottleneck. Motion-component leader.

companies.name: NSK
companies.thesis_note: Bearings + ball/roller screws; humanoid linear-actuation content. Auto-cycle exposed but robotics optionality.

companies.name: Nidec
companies.thesis_note: World's largest motor maker; frameless/BLDC for robotics + EV. Broad motion exposure; China competition rising.

companies.name: Inovance
companies.thesis_note: China's motion-control champion vertically integrating motors/drives/screws into humanoids. The China localization core.

companies.name: Sanhua Intelligent
companies.thesis_note: Exclusive Tier-1 Tesla Optimus actuator assembler ($685M order). The clearest listed Optimus supply-chain proxy.

companies.name: Tuopu Group
companies.thesis_note: Tesla Optimus 'T-Chain' Tier-1 actuator supplier (alongside Sanhua); auto-parts base (NVH, thermal, chassis) pivoting to humanoid linear/rotary actuators. A second listed Optimus actuator proxy.

companies.name: Shuanghuan Driveline
companies.thesis_note: Chinese precision-gear maker pivoting into RV reducers for industrial + humanoid joints (dedicated reducer line). Domestic challenger to Nabtesco on the heavy-joint side.

companies.name: Beite Technology
companies.thesis_note: Shanghai-listed; committed ¥1.85bn to a planetary-roller-screw plant — the costliest, most supply-constrained linear-actuator component. China second-source on the Optimus roller-screw bottleneck.

companies.name: Leaderdrive (Green Harmonic)
companies.thesis_note: China harmonic-reducer leader (绿的谐波 'Leaderdrive'; ~25%+ share); targeting Optimus supply via a 500K-unit/yr plant. STAR-listed localization beneficiary. (NB: same company sometimes mislabeled 'Green Harmonic' vs 'Leaderdrive'.)

companies.name: Fanuc
companies.thesis_note: Industrial robotics 'Big Four'; CNC + arms. Incumbent base; humanoid wave is optionality, China share-loss is risk.

companies.name: Yaskawa Electric
companies.thesis_note: Servo drives + industrial arms; motion-control breadth. Automation + humanoid component optionality.

companies.name: Regal Rexnord
companies.thesis_note: Owns Kollmorgen/Allied Motion frameless torque motors used in humanoids. US motion-component exposure.

companies.name: Schaeffler
companies.thesis_note: Bearings/motion major now selling a full humanoid joint module (gear + bearing + motor, ~€1,500/bot) and courting Figure + Agility; only ~18% China revenue. Citrini's clearest 'non-China humanoid design-win' play. Owns Ewellix (roller screws).

companies.name: Allient
companies.thesis_note: US motion-control platform (ElectroFlux radial / SA axial-flux motors); exited powersport/auto to focus on robotics, defense, medical. Engineering-led OEM motion cores, designing out rare-earth content. Re-rating on the motion supercycle.

companies.name: Wolong Electric
companies.thesis_note: Major global high-power motor maker; motors already used in Unitree robot dogs and applicable to large humanoid hip/knee/shoulder joints. China motor-supply-chain breadth.

companies.name: Ningbo Shuanglin
companies.thesis_note: Auto-supply-chain player scaling roller screws + linear actuators toward ~300K units/yr ahead of Tesla Optimus demand (each Optimus uses ~14 linear actuators). A concrete China scale-production signal.

companies.name: Tesla
companies.thesis_note: Optimus is the humanoid demand-setter — owns both the actuator-BOM design and the embodied-AI stack; Gen-3 reportedly ~70% China-sourced. The program that pulls the entire robotics supply chain. Diversified (auto/energy) = a robotics call-option, not a pure-play.

companies.name: Hyundai Motor
companies.thesis_note: Owns Boston Dynamics (Atlas) — premier Western humanoid R&D and Citrini's top-scored robotics OEM. Robotics is optionality on a global auto OEM.

companies.name: UBTech Robotics
companies.thesis_note: Cleanest listed pure-play humanoid maker; in-house servo actuators (0.2–200Nm), Walker S deployed in factories (BYD, Foxconn). China humanoid champion.

companies.name: Xiaomi
companies.thesis_note: CyberOne humanoid + CyberDog quadruped leverage Xiaomi's consumer-electronics + EV ecosystem and cost engineering; a 'de facto humanoid supplier' contender if it scales. Diversified, robotics is optionality.

companies.name: Estun Automation
companies.thesis_note: China industrial-robot + servo/motion-control champion (owns Trio UK, Cloos DE); core components in-house. Humanoid optionality off an industrial-arm base.

companies.name: ABB
companies.thesis_note: IRB industrial-robot family + ABB Robotics AI platform; deep actuator/control/integration stack. 'Big Four' incumbent; humanoid is optionality.

companies.name: Midea Group (KUKA)
companies.thesis_note: Owns KUKA ('Big Four' arms); RMB10bn Guangdong humanoid park. KUKA actuator IP + Midea cost curve = domestic humanoid optionality; diversified appliances base.

companies.name: Kawasaki Heavy Inds.
companies.thesis_note: Major industrial-robot maker (welding/assembly) with in-house servo know-how; Kaleido humanoid program. Diversified heavy-industry base, robotics optionality.

companies.name: Rainbow Robotics
companies.thesis_note: HUBO humanoid developer; Samsung lifted its stake to ~14% to accelerate biped R&D. Korea's Figure/Tesla-style peer with in-house actuation IP. (KOSDAQ-listed.)

companies.name: XPeng
companies.thesis_note: XPeng Robotics' IRON biped backed by a ¥100bn 20-yr commitment; shares EV supply chain + vision stack. China humanoid roll-out play; capital-intensive. (NYSE ADR.)

companies.name: Doosan Robotics
companies.thesis_note: Korean cobot leader and K-Humanoid Alliance member; multi-arm humanoid platform guided for 2026. Cobot base + humanoid optionality.

companies.name: Seiko Epson
companies.thesis_note: #1 SCARA robot maker; proprietary GYROPLUS motion sensing. Precision small-arm kinematics map to humanoid wrists/arms; diversified (printers) base.

companies.name: Teradyne
companies.thesis_note: Owns Universal Robots (cobot leader) + MiR (AMRs); UR arms power Amazon's Vulcan pick/stow robot — a potential $300-400M contract as Amazon automates ~80% of 14B hand-stowed items/yr. Core is semiconductor ATE (Advantest duopoly) + AI/HBM + custom-ASIC test, so robotics is one leg of a dual-catalyst name.

companies.name: Sony Group
companies.thesis_note: Dominant CMOS image sensors + OLEDoS micro-displays (Apple Vision Pro) + lasers. Multi-vertical sensing/display chokepoint.

companies.name: Hesai Group
companies.thesis_note: China lidar cost leader (>1.6M units 2025); Nvidia robotics partner. Fast-commoditizing but volume leader.

companies.name: Keyence
companies.thesis_note: Machine-vision + factory sensor powerhouse, ~50%+ margins. Automation breadth; premium quality compounder.

companies.name: Cognex
companies.thesis_note: Machine-vision pure-play; logistics + factory automation. Cyclical but robotics/vision secular tailwind.

companies.name: TDK
companies.thesis_note: InvenSense IMUs (ICM-42688 widely used in humanoids) + passives + batteries. Broad sensing/components exposure.

companies.name: Novanta
companies.thesis_note: Owns ATI 6-axis force/torque sensors — key to dexterous manipulation. Precision-sensing niche exposure.

companies.name: Keli Sensing
companies.thesis_note: China's largest traditional sensor maker, expanding into multi-axis (6-way) torque sensing for robot wrists/ankles — competing with ATI (Novanta) + Sunrise. Fills the force/torque chokepoint that gates dexterous manipulation.

companies.name: Allegro MicroSystems
companies.thesis_note: Hall-effect + current + magnetic position sensor ICs — 'in every joint' for precise motion control; sizes the humanoid-robot sensor SAM at >$10B (2030-35) with auto/robotics/DC cross-sell. Automotive-cycle exposed.

companies.name: Apex Dynamics
companies.thesis_note: Taiwan's #1 planetary gearbox maker — ships >450K/yr globally, second only to Germany's Wittenstein. Used in semi foundries, EV plants, food/beverage. Lower-cost rotary workhorse vs harmonic/RV — fits lower-cost humanoid joints.

companies.name: Timken
companies.thesis_note: Industrial bearings; owns Spinea, which ships ultra-compact cycloidal reducers viable for humanoid joints. US motion-component diversification play with humanoid optionality.

companies.name: Han's Laser
companies.thesis_note: Han's Laser — China industrial-automation conglomerate (laser-cell + Elfin cobots + 3D inspection). Cited as a Chinese motor/cobot challenger; humanoid integration optionality off a diversified automation base.

companies.name: Kinco Electric
companies.thesis_note: China frameless / servo motor challenger to Kollmorgen and Nidec; named alongside VEICHI and Han's as the China motor cohort. STAR-listed motion-control localization play.

companies.name: Hota Industrial
companies.thesis_note: Taiwan precision-gear maker — sits alongside Apex Dynamics as the Taiwan planetary-gearbox cohort; Tesla/Optimus drivetrain optionality given the supply-chain shift away from China.

companies.name: RBC Bearings
companies.thesis_note: US precision bearings maker; named alongside Schaeffler and Timken as the Western bearing cohort. Defense-budget tailwind + humanoid optionality; not a pure-play.

companies.name: Cloudflare
companies.chain_layer: CDN + Workers + agentic infra (zero-trust, pay-per-crawl, x402)
companies.thesis_note: Most comprehensive agentic-infra play: Workers (distributed compute), Durable Objects (state), pay-per-crawl, NET-dollar stablecoin for agentic commerce, Browser Rendering, signed agent traffic, Firewall for AI. Citrini June: 'beat + guide raise + 20% headcount cut, sold off' — still bullish on quality + exposure.

companies.name: Akamai
companies.thesis_note: CDN pivoting to AI compute (Akamai Inference Cloud Oct 2025, $250M capex). API security +100% YoY. Citrini June: $1.8B 7-yr frontier-lab compute commitment; +80% YTD. The CDN-to-compute-delivery thesis.

companies.name: Fastly
companies.thesis_note: Edge compute + AI Accelerator (semantic caching cuts inference cost/latency). WebAssembly Compute platform. Citrini June: security +47%, compute +67%, RPO +63%. Highest convexity among CDNs.

companies.name: Twilio
companies.thesis_note: CPaaS for agents: ConversationRelay (out-of-the-box voice AI), Segment (15-yr customer-data moat), A2H protocol. Already handles 85% of own inbound sales via AI. Citrini June: trades >30x fwd.

companies.name: Bandwidth
companies.thesis_note: Owns physical telephony infrastructure (PSTN interconnects, carrier licenses, number portability) in 60+ countries; rented by MSFT/GOOG/AMZN. OpenAI Realtime API integration. Citrini June: up ~300%; won Salesforce Agentforce contract.

companies.name: Sinch
companies.thesis_note: Swedish CPaaS un-rerated catch-up to TWLO/BAND. EU AI Act August 2026 reasoning-log requirement could be a regulatory tailwind. Smaller / cheaper exposure to the same agentic-comms wave.

companies.name: SailPoint
companies.thesis_note: Identity governance lifecycle — provisions and revokes access for every identity (human + non-human + AI agent). Citrini June: ~11% of governed identities are already non-human; platformization angle vs PANW's CyberArk acquisition.

companies.name: Palo Alto Networks
companies.thesis_note: Platformization: Chronosphere acq (observability) + CyberArk acq (~$25B, PAM/agent identity). Zero Standing Privilege architecture for agentic workflows. Citrini's preferred cyber-platform play for the agentic era.

companies.name: Datadog
companies.thesis_note: Observability for monitoring + billing of ephemeral agent workloads. Citrini June: non-AI segment +25%; upgraded view post-earnings. Telemetry IS financial plumbing in agent-native architectures.

companies.name: Dynatrace
companies.thesis_note: Observability + AIOps platform. Healthy print; Citrini June names it as a second observability pick alongside DDOG.

companies.name: JFrog
companies.thesis_note: DevOps platformization → unified dev environment incl. model/artifact registry. Reference designs for AI-native dev. Citrini June: noted as DevOps platformization play.

companies.name: VeriSign
companies.thesis_note: Authoritative .com/.net registry — 450B DNS queries/day. Every agent web request starts with DNS resolution; agentic workflows fan out to 10 lookups vs 1 for human. 67% operating margins, virtually zero CAC.

companies.name: A10 Networks
companies.thesis_note: Manages the (now-scarce) IPv4 address table via NAT (Thunder CGN) + builds IPv6 transition infrastructure. Every persistent agent session needs an addressable endpoint. Cybersecurity wrapper growing.

companies.name: CoreWeave
companies.thesis_note: Neocloud — $99.4B RPO Q1 2026, 1GW+ active capacity. $21B Meta expansion, $6B Jane Street cloud commitment + $1B equity. Citrini June: missed Q2 guide ('supply constrained and operationally difficult') — caution flag despite the demand.

companies.name: Hewlett Packard Enterprise
companies.thesis_note: Server systems + Juniper acq (networking +152% YoY). HPE Private Cloud full-stack subscription. Picks up agentic on-prem demand.

companies.name: DigitalOcean
companies.thesis_note: Managed cloud for SMBs / digital-native AI startups. High-touch partner vs hyperscalers' DIY. Re-accelerating topline as DNE/agentic-startup mix climbs.

companies.name: Jabil
companies.thesis_note: Diversified EMS; Intelligent Infrastructure segment (robotics capital equipment + AI servers) led recent upside. Citrindex Robotics basket member; broader AI-server EMS exposure alongside CLS.

companies.name: Huber+Suhner
companies.thesis_note: OCS + RF connectivity; record CHF432M backlog; scaling Polish capacity 5x. Critical player alongside Lumentum in Google's MEMS OCS / Project Apollo TPU pods. EU Chips Act 2.0 beneficiary.

companies.name: Canatu
companies.thesis_note: Sole CNT pellicle pure-play; ASML supplier (CNT pellicles needed for High-NA EUV reticle protection). ~€300M cap, ~€15M TTM revenue — high risk / high reward. EU Chips Act 2.0 microcap.

companies.name: Nordic Semiconductor
companies.thesis_note: Only EU fabless low-power wireless pure-play; Bluetooth LE ~40% share. Edge-AI SoCs for IoT/wearables (the on-device inference inflection's silicon supplier). EU Chips Act 2.0 beneficiary.

companies.name: Infineon
companies.thesis_note: European power-semi major; SiC + silicon power for auto + AI 800V-HVDC. Prior EU Chips Act 1.0 winner; positioned for 2.0. Acquired AMS-OSRAM sensor unit (€570M).

companies.name: Silicon Motion
companies.thesis_note: Flash controller specialist — central to the 'past the DRAM tax' thesis (controller optimization is one of 3 paths to offload weight storage from scarce DRAM to NAND/HBF). Edge-AI memory controller content rising.

companies.name: Ouster
companies.thesis_note: Rev8/L4 silicon color LiDAR; Nvidia Jetson/DRIVE integration. SPAD-SoC architecture — robotics + autonomy. Citrini's preferred LiDAR pure-play alongside Hesai.

companies.name: Aeva Technologies
companies.thesis_note: Atlas 4D LiDAR — frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW). Daimler Truck Level-4 road tests; Torc partnership targeting 2027 series production. Differentiated 4D physics vs ToF lidar.

companies.name: Axcelis Technologies
companies.thesis_note: Ion implantation tools — pivotal for SiC doping (the EV-cohort capacity now inheriting AI 800V-HVDC demand). Mid-merger with Veeco (VECO).

companies.name: Power Integrations
companies.thesis_note: High-voltage power-conversion ICs; AC-to-DC + DC-DC conversion. AI rack power transition (800V HVDC) demand; Citrindex Dynamic AI basket member.

companies.name: Sunny Optical
companies.thesis_note: China's largest optical lens + camera module maker — smartphones, autos, AR/VR, robotics. Multi-vertical optics exposure including robotics-vision angle. Citrindex Robotics basket member.

companies.name: Victory Giant Technology
companies.thesis_note: High-layer-count PCB maker for AI servers — sits at the AI-server BOM intersection of CCL + HVLP copper foil. Citrindex Dynamic AI basket. China PCB ascent.

companies.name: Silex Microsystems
companies.thesis_note: Swedish pure-play MEMS foundry (now owned by Sai MicroElectronics 300456.SZ). Fabs the MEMS mirror chips Lumentum uses in Google's TPU OCS pods. EU Chips Act 2.0 + photonics enabler crossover.

companies.name: Ambiq Micro
companies.thesis_note: Sub-threshold ultra-low-power MCUs — sips microamps. Critical for always-on AI sensing at the battery-constrained edge (wearables, hearables, medical patches).

companies.name: Sensata Technologies
companies.thesis_note: Industrial pressure / position / temperature / current sensors. Broad sensing portfolio with robotics + automation cross-sell. Citrindex Robotics basket.

companies.name: Synaptics
companies.thesis_note: Touch / fingerprint / display-driver / audio ICs. IoT + edge-AI human-interface SoCs. Citrindex Robotics basket.

companies.name: Knowles
companies.thesis_note: MEMS microphones + balanced armature speakers + specialty capacitors. Voice-AI hardware angle + hearable / earbud content. Citrindex Robotics basket.

companies.name: Arteris
companies.thesis_note: Network-on-Chip (NoC) interconnect IP — sits inside SoC designs from custom-ASIC / robotics-silicon designers. License-based recurring revenue. Citrindex Robotics basket.

companies.name: CEVA
companies.thesis_note: Licensable DSP, AI, Bluetooth/5G IP for edge SoCs. Royalties per shipped chip. Citrindex Dynamic AI basket.

companies.name: Intuitive Surgical
companies.thesis_note: Surgical robotics leader; razor-razorblade installed base. Adjacent end-market for precision robotics.

companies.name: Hamamatsu Photonics
companies.thesis_note: Japan's photodetector leader (photodiodes, SiPM/SPAD, PMTs) — receivers for lidar + machine-vision + medical/industrial sensing. A quiet photonics-sensing chokepoint across robotics, autonomy and instrumentation.

companies.name: Analog Devices
companies.thesis_note: High-end MEMS IMUs (ADIS) + precision analog/signal-chain and ToF sensing front-ends for robots, industrial and autos. Broad, high-quality exposure across the robot nervous system.

companies.name: Orbbec
companies.thesis_note: China 3D-vision specialist — structured-light + ToF depth cameras for robots/embodied AI (Nvidia robotics-ecosystem partner). Depth perception for manipulation + navigation.

companies.name: Melexis
companies.thesis_note: Belgian magnetic/Hall position + current sensor specialist — joint-position and motor-commutation sensing for robots and autos. Automotive-cycle exposed; robotics optionality.

companies.name: Ambarella
companies.thesis_note: Edge-AI vision/perception SoCs (CVflow). Used in robotics + ADAS + drones. Cited alongside Broadcom/MediaTek/Marvell as a candidate for fixed-function VLA ASICs as embodied AI matures. Smaller pure-play exposure to robot/edge inference.

companies.name: Himax Technologies
companies.thesis_note: LCoS micro-displays + display driver ICs. Hidden CPO play: makes the nanoimprint optics-block/micro-lens-array inside the fiber-array unit for TSMC COUPE (with FOCI) — a Nvidia Rubin-era ramp. Also the likely Apple smart-glasses supplier (WiseEye low-power sensing, LCoS, WLO waveguides). Non-driver segment is the growth vector.

companies.name: BOE Technology
companies.thesis_note: China display giant scaling OLEDoS + microLED for MR/AR. Volume + cost; China display ascendancy play.

companies.name: AU Optronics
companies.thesis_note: Panel maker pivoting to microLED + automotive/AR. Taiwan display transition exposure.

companies.name: ams OSRAM
companies.thesis_note: microLED + emitters + optical sensing. AR/automotive photonics; restructuring story with microLED optionality.

companies.name: MicroVision
companies.thesis_note: Laser beam scanning + lidar. Speculative AR/automotive display-tech option; high risk.

companies.name: Corning
companies.thesis_note: High-index glass for AR waveguides + optical fiber for AI clusters. Materials chokepoint bordering the hard-assets map.

companies.name: Vuzix
companies.thesis_note: Waveguide manufacturer + enterprise AR OEM; acquired ex-Google waveguide lab. Speculative AR pure-play.

companies.name: Qualcomm
companies.thesis_note: De-facto AR/XR SoC (Snapdragon AR) — the smart-glasses compute chokepoint. Diversified; AR is the call-option.

companies.name: Meta Platforms
companies.thesis_note: Ray-Ban Display breakout + Orion; the AI-glasses category creator + biggest AR R&D spender. Drives the whole AR BOM.

companies.name: Goertek
companies.thesis_note: Built the Ray-Ban Display light engine; dominant AR/VR device assembler. China assembly chokepoint for smart glasses.

companies.name: Luxshare Precision
companies.thesis_note: Major Apple/AR device assembler + components. China precision-assembly leverage to AR/wearables ramp.

companies.name: SICC (Tianyue)
companies.thesis_note: SiC substrates; emerging SiC AR waveguides (Meta Orion). Verify ticker. Speculative materials-chokepoint option.
